sentences.text: THIS WP IS FILED UNDER ARTICLES 226 & 227 OF THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA, PRAYING TO QUASH THE PRELIMINARY NOTIFICATION UNDER ANNEX-H DATED 15.04.1997 ISSUED BY R-2 AND FINAL NOTIFICATION DATED 25.11.2005 UNDER ANNEX-J ISSUED BY R-1; OR IN THE ALTERNATIVE FOR A DECLARATION THAT AQUISITION PROCEEDINGS INITIATE THAT THE PRELIMINARY NOTIFICATION DATED 15.09.1997 AND THE FINAL NOTIFICATION DATED 25.11.2005 UNDER ANNEX-H AND J HAVE LAPSED; AWARD COST AND ETC.

THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

This writ petition is filed seeking for following reliefs:
(a) Issue a writ of certiorari or any other writ, order, quashing the Preliminary Notification under Annexure-H bearing No.CP92SPQ97 dated 15.04.1997 issued by respondent no.2 and Final Notification dated 25.11.2005 under Annexure-J bearing No.C1294SPQ2005 issued by respondent no.1.

OR In the alternative for a direction that acquisition proceedings initiate that the Preliminary Notification dated 15.09.1997 and the Final Notification dated 25.11.2005 under Annexures- H and J have lapsed.
(b) Award cost and other reliefs deems fit under the circumstances of the case, in the interest of justice.

2. Sri B.B. Patil and Sri H.N. Narendra Dev, learned counsel for respondents no.3 to 8 submitted that this writ petition is filed seeking for quashing of Preliminary Notification and Final Notification for acquisition of land bearing Sy.no.244/13B of Bananduru Village, Bidadi Hobli, Ramanagara Taluk, measuring 3 acres 11 guntas on ground of having lapsed NC: 2023:KHC:44669 in view of Section 24(2) of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short 'RFCTLARR Act').
3.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
It was submitted that Division Bench of this Court in W.A.no.1451/2018, disposed of on 02.03.2021 had held that in case of acquisition under Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act,
Bangalore Development Act or Karnataka Urban Development Authorities Act, acquisition being under a special enactment, there cannot be a challenge by reference to Section 24(2) of RFCTLARR Act, 2013, by referring to decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of INDORE DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY v/s MANOHARLAL AND OTHERS, reported in AIR 2020 SC 1496. It was pointed out Sri Venugopal vs The State Of Karnataka on 8 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199454199/

that in respect of very same acquisition, petitioners had earlier filed W.P.no.41241/2010, wherein petitioners challenge against acquisition proceedings was turned-down and liberty was reserved to file application for reference under Section 18 of Land Acquisition Act,1894.
4.

It was further pointed out that as per Annexure-R2 produced along with statement of objection filed by KIADB, SLAO had deposited award amount before Reference Court for NC:
2023:KHC:44669 adjudication of dispute between petitioners and respondents no.6 to 8.
It was also pointed out that legal notice at Annexure-M would indicate that petitioners had expressed interest in receiving compensation.
Therefore, present writ petition filed challenging acquisition on any count would not be tenable.

5. In reply, Sri Lakshminarayana, learned counsel for petitioner no.2(A) submitted that petitioners did not want to question acquisition, but were interested in having been land identified since acquired extent of 3 acres 11 guntas was only a portion out of total extent of 15 acres.

6. Heard learned counsel and perused writ petition record.
7.
In view of above submission and decisions relied upon by learned counsel for respondents, writ petition insofar as challenge to acquisition would not be tenable.

8. Insofar as petitioners' concern that land acquired has not been identified, since it is stated that reference under Sections 30 and 31 is pending before Reference Court, wherein NC:
2023:KHC:44669 petitioners as well respondents no.6 to 8 were parties, said concern could also be addressed and resolved.
9.

Hence, writ petition is disposed of relegating dispute insofar as extent and identification of acquired land to be decided by Reference Court, if necessary by framing appropriate additional issue by permitting parties to lead evidence on same.
Parties are directed to co-operate for early conclusion of proceedings before Reference Court.
